topic_and_scope: A focused analysis of how the human microbiome influences primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) through data-driven AI and mechanism-driven modeling, highlighting future research directions to advance causal understanding and clinical translation.
main_themes: Data-driven AI and mathematical modeling reveal associations and potential causal links between gut microbiome composition and POAG features (e.g., IOP, disease progression).
There is a critical need to integrate data-driven AI approaches with mechanism-based (physics-inspired) models to uncover causal pathways in the gut–eye axis.
Gaps in data quality, population diversity, interpretability, and ethical governance limit generalizability and clinical adoption of microbiome–glaucoma insights.
main_findings: Data-driven methods, including Mendelian randomization and machine learning, have identified associations and potential causal links between specific microbial taxa (e.g., Lachnospiraceae, Lactococcus) and POAG severity or intraocular pressure (IOP).

Mechanism-driven models are underutilized in microbiome–glaucoma research, and integrating AI-enhanced data-driven analyses with physics-based simulations could yield deeper causal mechanistic insights and more actionable predictions.

key_gaps.description: Explicit gap: lack of integration between data-driven AI models and mechanism-driven (physics-based) simulations of the gut–eye axis.
Implied gap: variability in study design, sampling methods, and sequencing, along with small, non-diverse cohorts, limiting data quality, generalizability, and causal inference.

future_directions.title: Develop hybrid AI-mechanistic models of the gut–eye axis
future_directions.rationale: The literature underscores the potential of combining data-driven AI with mechanism-based simulations. Build hybrid models that couple AI-driven descriptions of microbiome patterns with physics- and biology-based representations of metabolite transport, immune signaling, and retinal neurodegeneration. Concrete steps include collecting multi-omics and longitudinal clinical data to parameterize the models, implementing them in a Virtual Laboratory, and validating predictions against independent cohorts and preclinical systems. Use these models to simulate interventions (diet, probiotics, targeted therapies) and predict effects on IOP, inflammatory markers, and RNFL/optic nerve outcomes.

future_directions.title: Establish large, diverse, longitudinal POAG cohorts with standardized microbiome sampling
future_directions.rationale: To address data quality and generalizability issues, launch multi-center cohorts with harmonized protocols for gut, oral, and ocular microbiome sampling, plus comprehensive phenotyping (IOP dynamics, optic nerve imaging, inflammatory markers). Include diverse populations across geographies, ages, and diets, with repeated sampling to capture temporal dynamics. Ensure open data sharing and standardized metadata to enable cross-cohort replication and meta-analyses. This foundation is essential for robust causal inference and model validation.

future_directions.title: Apply and replicate causal inference across cohorts to identify robust microbiome drivers of POAG
future_directions.rationale: Building on MR findings, systematically apply causal inference frameworks (MR, bidirectional MR, and other causal methods) across independent populations to confirm taxa that influence IOP and glaucoma progression. Use GWAS and metagenomic data to identify solid instrumental variables and test reverse causation (IOP/retinal outcomes influencing microbiome). Replication across cohorts will strengthen the evidence base for microbiome-targeted interventions.

future_directions.title: Identify and clinically validate microbiome biomarkers for POAG risk and progression
future_directions.rationale: Leverage consistent taxa signals (e.g., Lachnospiraceae, Lactococcus) to develop robust biomarker panels. Validate these panels in independent cohorts and translate them into practical assays (qPCR panels, targeted sequencing) suitable for risk stratification and monitoring disease trajectory. Integrate biomarker data with clinical risk factors to refine prediction models and guide personalized management strategies.

future_directions.title: Characterize mechanistic pathways linking gut dysbiosis to ocular neuroinflammation
future_directions.rationale: Investigate the LPS-TLR4 axis and other immune pathways connecting gut-derived signals to retinal tissue. Use animal models (germ-free and gnotobiotic systems) and ex vivo assays to measure microbial metabolite flux, systemic and ocular inflammatory responses, and retinal neuroprotection or injury. Translate mechanistic insights into targeted interventions that could mitigate neuroinflammation and optic neuropathy in POAG.

future_directions.title: Develop and validate explainable AI tools for clinical decision support in POAG
future_directions.rationale: Address the 'black box' nature of AI by building interpretable models with transparent feature attributions linking microbiome features to risk and progression. Create clinician-facing dashboards that integrate microbiome signatures with IOP, imaging, and inflammatory markers. Validate effectiveness in real-world clinical settings and assess impact on decision-making, patient trust, and outcomes.

future_directions.title: Evaluate microbiome-modulating interventions in preclinical and early human studies
future_directions.rationale: Based on causal and mechanistic findings, test interventions (dietary modification, probiotics, prebiotics, or targeted antibiotics) in appropriate models and in early-phase clinical trials. Primary endpoints should include safety, changes in microbiome composition, alterations in systemic and ocular inflammatory markers, and indications of impact on IOP and retinal biomarkers. Negative results should inform refinement of targets and trial design.
